text:
**Card spending: no Monzo fee.** When you pay abroad with a UK Monzo personal debit card, Monzo uses Mastercard’s exchange rate without adding a markup. If a shop or cash machine offers to charge you in pounds, **choose the local currency** so you get Mastercard’s rate rather than the operator’s. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/help/travelling/understanding-fees))

**Cash withdrawals: Monzo charges 3% on the amount above your fee-free allowance.** The allowances apply over a rolling 30-day period, not a calendar month. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/help/travelling/understanding-fees))

| Your Monzo account | UK and EEA combined | Abroad outside the EEA |
|---|---:|---:|
| Free account, not your main bank | £400 | £200 |
| Free account, Monzo is your main bank | Unlimited fee-free | £200 |
| Extra | Unlimited fee-free | £200 |
| Plus | Unlimited fee-free | £400 |
| Premium, Perks or Max | Unlimited fee-free | £600 |

The EEA is the EU plus Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway. To check which allowance applies to you, tap the **three dots** on your account in the Monzo app and select **Fees and allowances**. Even within your allowance, the ATM operator may charge its own fee. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/help/travelling/understanding-fees))
